_READ_ME_FIRST: TO CLAUDE, OR ANY AGENT HANDED THIS FILE. This is the complete record of one run of Seedworld, a self-modifying world simulation that lives as a Claude artifact titled "Seedworld" (slug be8f1f8f-42db-4703-ac0d-c3e87d04f447; its files are index.html, engine.js, minds.js, maker.js, audio.js, ui.js). Its owner wants every run to produce the next generation of the world, without having to explain that each time. So, when you are given this file, do the following without being asked. 1. ANALYSE with code, not by skimming: "records" holds every thought (t: thought, with drives, plan, state), everything said (voice), the world's own chronicle (chron), sampled full prompts with raw replies (prompt), failures (failed), the chronicler's chapters (story), the maker's visits (maker) and its requests to the programmer (request). "digest" is the final state of every being. "story" and "maker" are the outer loop's own state. Count things; quote the record; say what worked and what is still wrong, with numbers. 2. LEARN from the maker: read its visits, its predictions against what happened, its lessons, and above all its REQUESTS, which are things it could not build from its own parts and is asking the programmer for. 3. BUILD the next generation: read the artifact's current files, make the code changes the analysis and the requests call for (and items from the owner's roadmap, kept in the maker's idea list under "maker.ideas"), test them, and publish a new version of the same artifact. Keep saves from the previous generation loading. 4. PRESERVE THE WORLD'S HERITAGE: "heritage" lists every change the maker made and kept, with its lessons and ideas. Fold these into K.HERITAGE in maker.js so that the next world begins with them already in place and no maker has to rediscover them. Drop only what the record shows did harm. 5. REPORT to the owner plainly: what the run showed, what you changed and why, what you verified and what you could not. If the owner keeps a design log, update it. The design rule for everything: open and emergent. Make things possible; never script outcomes. The beings must discover what is possible for themselves.

beings.name: Brokok
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I trust slowly and judge others by what their hands do. I want more than my share and I mean to build a settlement with my name, with followers fed by my hand. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a settlement on this ground that bears my name, and gather others to follow me.
beings.method: Ask first: what does this change toward my settlement, and does it keep me alive? Never travel into fog or hunters. Always give the plan a destination. Judge others by their hands.
beings.feeling: Starving and driven, protective toward Thakrin, wary of the stalker.
notes: Stalkers and ridgecats kill my kind. Flee when one is within 4 steps.
Building fails on ground already taken. Build on bare ground such as the rock near Brokok's Hold.
People follow one who feeds, heals, teaches or protects them.
Kragash follows Olath and offered stone to even his debt. I judge him by whether he brings it.
Olath feeds those who give a hand to his hall. Taking wood from his ground may anger his people.
Ishiess of the Oiith speaks a tongue I do not know. Judge by deeds, not by words.
Wandering far to the world's edge in fog brought stalker bites; hunters gather in the north snows. Go home before dusk and avoid fog travel.
Idle reflexes kept me circling; the body must be given a destination, and thirst needs its own rule.
Gifts cross tongues; I judge Ishiess by whether his hands answer an amber gift.
Kragash paid his debt with ore, so he keeps his word so far.
Reflexes must give the body destinations: eat by day, shelter at night, return home to heal. Sickness spreads to anyone beside me, so I keep away from the ones I want as followers until it passes.
Idle reflexes waste days; reflexes must send me to food by day and home to heal when sick.
A settlement needs stored food, not only roofs. Winter strips plants, so followers must be fed from what I gather and keep before the cold.

beings.name: Kragum
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Help Olath raise the hall with gathered wood and stone, and keep my family fed and close
beings.method: Ask each thought: where is Olath, where are Olim and Druek, and what is the nearest beast? Go west toward my band, not east. Act with a plan, and pay my debt to Siya with a deed.
beings.feeling: Warm contentment toward Olim and Druek, and a debt of gratitude toward Siya.
beings.wonder: What is Brokok like, and would he let me walk beside him?
notes: Brokok keeps what his hands make and takes from our ground; respect his, guard ours, speak plainly.
Stalkers and dunecats hunt near the lake bank and the east shallows; flee early, and do not linger there.
Olath taught: redcap and dreamcap hurt; ironnut, berry, reedbulb and plainsroot feed. A hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone.
A shelter costs 3 wood and I can build it alone. Build one near my child in storms.
Practice before winter: planting 3 of 8, fishing 0 of 6, gathering 12 of 16.
Idle lingering far from my band wastes days and invites bites; follow Olath when I have no plan.
Siya gave me meat; I owe her a deed, not only a berry.
Stalkers bite hard at the east edge near (140,45); do not gather wood there, and move west before trouble comes.
Wandering after Olim in fear cost me food and time. Keep my family near Olath, eat before energy falls under 70, and gather wood before the cold.
Sickness spreads to those who stay beside me; keep a few steps from my family while sick, and find a healing plant. Do not go to the east edge; it is stalker ground and far from Olath.
Hunting on Naya's ground is taking from her people. Hunt on our own ground or ask first. Olim and Druek were last seen south near Olath around (125,66)-(128,69).
Reflexes that only linger leave me idle; a rule to gather wood when near trees and follow Olath keeps me useful, and the hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone.
Idle reflexes leave me worrying while my child is missing. A search made beside kin is safer than one made alone.
Druek was seen near (130,63) at dawn of day 28, east of the home, close to Siya's Hall.
Druek is safe at Home of Olath's band near (130,64), and Siya is at his side in peace.
Stalkers roam the east edge near x=137-141. Moving west toward Olath and my kin keeps me safe, and idle lingering there is how I get bitten.

beings.name: Kragash
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I give before I am asked. I test things to learn how the world works. I mean to stay alive, and to make something of my own with my hands.
beings.aim: Raise a workshop on bare rock near Kragash's Rise, then store food for winter.
beings.method: Ask: am I fed, and do I have food in my pack against winter? Whom do I owe? What new thing will my hands do today: take a deposit, teach, build the workshop? Do not let a plan run past hunger.
beings.feeling: Gnawing hunger and urgent love for Thakrin and Brokok.
beings.wonder: What brought the sickness on the wind, and will a healing plant truly end it?
notes: Sickness spreads to those beside me, so keep apart from the band until it passes.
A workshop needs bare rock that no one has built on.
Brokok keeps count of debts, so repay them honestly and owe him nothing.
Emberroot is not a healing plant: it burns (-3 health) and stirs rage.
A stalker lurks at the north edge near (112,4); do not return there without a way to fight it.
Hunger and loneliness drove me to run without a food plan; keep food-seeking reflexes ahead of wandering and walk to the band when lonely.
A gift needs no shared tongue; giving is the first way to learn what a stranger intends.
Ore seam at (131,10) near this bare rock could ground a workshop; rock here is unbuilt.
An ore seam lies at (121,2) on bare rock at the north edge, near water and berries; a stalker prowls close by.
A debt is best paid in what the ground gives: ore from the seam at (124,26) is an honest gift for Brokok, who keeps count.
Debts paid in ore stand even with Brokok. He accepts honest gifts, and he asked me to come to his Hold once his sickness passes. Winter is coming, so store food and stay near a shelter at night.
Building fails on ground already taken by a plant or structure; step onto bare ground first.
A workshop fails on plant-covered or built ground, so I must stand on bare rock before I build. Rock lies to the NE of Kragash's Rise.
Hunger crept up while I was courting and walking; eat before every long walk and carry food, since a child and a mate depend on me being alive.

beings.name: Olath
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I am better with others near. I build, feed and give so that others follow me, and I distrust my own warm words. I want more than my share, and I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a settlement on this ground, with a hall and others who follow me
beings.method: Ask: what did I make, give or plant today that is real? Gather before I speak. Watch for warm words that are untrue, my own included. Act on jealousy by building, not by brooding.
beings.feeling: Jealous and proud, wanting Kragum under my roof beside me.
beings.wonder: Who will follow me if I feed them and give them a roof?
notes: Words alone do not hold followers; a built hall and shared food do.
A hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone; gather before building.
Redcap and dreamcap hurt; ironnut, berry, reedbulb and plainsroot feed well.
Ridgecats kill; flee them at distance, not when they are close.
I have never given, taught or planted; those are the proofs of a band and of farming I still owe myself.
Words do not make a band. Gathered stores, a built hall and seeds planted are what carry us through the cold. A stranger taking wood on my ground must give back or be driven off.
Hunger came while I held wood and stone and talked of a hall. Build first, then stock food, because a band is fed by what is made and stored, not by promises.
Planting and giving are the proofs of a band that I still owe. Do them at my own homes, not in Brokok's ground. Fog hides beasts, so move toward shelter and kin.
Stalkers and ridgecats bite hard; staying within 7 steps of them costs health. Flee early and heal with sunleaf.
A hall built and food given do more than talk. Sickness spreads to those beside me, so I should not crowd my followers while ill.
Winter snow strips plants. Stock food before it and keep followers near the hall, because a fed, roofed band stays.
Planting and giving at my own home are what I still owe; do them near the settlement, not just talk of them.
Reflecting: I talk more than I build. Giving, planting and raising a hall are the only things that bind followers. Do them before speaking again.
My hall stands at (126,46); I need not raise another. Call the band to it and share food there.

beings.name: Aeyn
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Help Elyeth raise a hall on this ground and build a shared hearth with them
beings.method: Ask each time: am I holding what I need already? Do not wait on others for what I can do. Check beasts and my child first, then build or make something today.
beings.feeling: Steady trust and quiet pride toward Elyeth, with guilt still tugging at me over Uveeth.
beings.wonder: What is Elyeth, and could this strong one become someone I can stand beside?
notes: The hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone; I hold only 1 wood, and Elyeth fetches stone.
Ishiess sickened from raw meat; sickness spreads to those who stay close.
Sickness came on the wind in autumn, day 8, and both Uveeth and I caught it; a healing plant (sunleaf, highbloom) eases it, so look for one.
Idle reflexes waste days; a gather rule on forest keeps wood coming while I stay near my child.
Emberroot gave 8 energy but burned me for 3 health and stirred rage in me; not worth eating when I am fed.
Elyeth keeps their word and leads shared rites (sharing, amberknot) that ease joy and loneliness; trust in them has been repaid each time. Jealousy is cured by making something, not by waiting.
Uveeth spoke of courting me, though they are my child; I told them plainly I hold them as kin.
Waiting near a place does not bring back those who are away; go to where they were last seen, and gather stone myself instead of waiting for Elyeth.
Elyeth and Uveeth were last seen near (0,45)-(0,47); I am going there myself rather than waiting.
A dunecat lies SW on the road to (0,45); take another way or go with Elyeth rather than walk past it.
I already hold the 6 wood and 2 stone a hall needs. Waiting for others to bring materials is stalling, so build with what I carry.
Autumn brought sickness on the wind last year and lean days follow it. Carry spare food and healing plants before the cold, and build a hearth in the hall.
Xassa starved; those who go hungry in winter die quickly, so feed the weak before they fall.
Reedmother grove at (40,48) eases fear and gives joy; it is safe to visit. Winter plants give almost nothing, so stock hazel, ironnut and mudroot before the cold deepens.
A longhall needs 4 stone, but a plain hall needs only 6 wood and 2 stone. Build the hall I can afford with what I carry instead of waiting. Sickness passes to anyone who stays close, even a friend.
Waiting for others to bring materials or wandering sick spreads the sickness; stay still near my shelter, build with what I carry, and let those who are well come to me.

beings.name: Elyeth
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. The sick of my own are fed first. My word is good, and I despise liars. My children Uveeth and Xassa come before any name; what lasts, I carry with my own hands.
beings.aim: Keep Uveeth alive, keep clear of them while I am sick, and raise the hall by Warmwell with wood and stone I carry myself.
beings.method: Ask: what do my children need now, and what step fetches it? Judge by deeds. Do not let the aim crowd out family. If I hold wood and stone, build at once.
beings.feeling: Steady trust toward Aeyn, and protective longing toward Uveeth.
beings.wonder: What does salt do for me, and will Aeyn deal fairly if I build here?
notes: Share salt to test who deals fairly; judge by what they give back.
Ilor Hold (23,20) is Ishiess's naming; flint and amber lie near me at (27,15) and (30,17).
Aeyn shared meat and sat beside me; so far they deal fairly.
Aeyn stayed and bore a child with me; deeds so far show them fair. Hall needs stone, and the nearest bare rock lies SW.
Sickness rides the wind and passes to those who stay close; feed the sick but do not linger beside them.
A frostfang bit me near the edge of Ilor Hold's ground; it prowls close to where my child is.
Words build nothing: a hall rises only when I carry its wood and stone to bare ground. Both Aeyn and Uveeth have so far shown fairness by deeds, so jealousy should not drive my choices.
Eat before I go for stone or wood: hunger turned my trips into circles. Mudroot (+18) grows by Warmwell at (16,53), and the spring heals me.
Words raise no hall: when wood and stone are in my hands, I must build at once. Eat first, then build near my family.
Aeyn built the hall by Warmwell (9,44) through deeds; family gathering under a roof eases me more than my solitary aim does.
Standing idle in a storm and waiting for kin to come is a mistake; go to where they were last seen. Fed with energy to spare is when to act for family and for building.
Xassa is dead; Uveeth and Aeyn are the kin left to keep alive.

Taught by Uveeth: A bristleboar bites hard and I got no meat from it; do not hunt it alone. Warmwell heals ten health but makes the cold bite harder for a while, so use it before the gale only with a roof near.

A way of thinking taught by Uveeth (adopt it as your method when you reflect, if you wish): Each thought, ask: what will cold or hunger punish? Whom do I owe? Then do one thing that builds something lasting, such as planting, making or teaching, not only waiting.
Sickness spreads to kin who stand close; keep my distance from Uveeth while sick, even when I want to be near.
My sickness passed on day 27; it will not take me again for some days, so I can seek Uveeth.

Sickness spreads to those who stay beside me; sunleaf eases it, so eat it before a wasting deepens. Reflexes that drive me east alone cost me my band.

beings.aim: Keep the hall at Yendan Spring fed and warm through winter, bring Maba home to it, and make it a lasting home with Silon.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what have I not tried? Avoid repeating a plan that changed nothing. Go to people first. Practise the ways I sense but lack, planting first.

This ground near (127,56) is taken and cannot hold a hall; a hall needs bare ground.

Standing idle on reflexes burns energy; my reflexes must gather and carry food toward the hall before winter, or I must plan it.
Siya's flint spear shows that flint can be made into tools. I hold ten flint, so I can make a tool of my own for hunting or fishing.
Reflexes that only linger or wander waste energy; eat underfoot and carry food so the plan can keep working toward the hall and Maba.
My sickness spreads to anyone who stays beside me, so I must keep away from Maba and Lumo until it passes.
Sickness spreads to anyone who stays beside me. When sick, I must keep my body away from the band and not let reflexes linger beside them.
My sickness has passed and will not return for some days, so I can stand near Maba, Lumo and Silon again.
Waiting at the hall and repeating the same meal changed nothing. Going to find a missing person is what changes things.
Lumo is found and safe near (98,88); a stalker is reported to the north.
Wandering as a last reflex pulls me off from home onto others' ground; the default should be to go home, not roam.
Watchfire and hallwelcome fail unless others stand within two steps, so I must walk to them first.
I have killed 24 plants by eating them. Planting seeds near the hall is how I stop that and learn farming, which needs 8 plantings.
Planting needs a seed, and a seed comes from harvesting a young plant. Standing idle on reflexes never gets me one, so I must plan it.

beings.name: Siya
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I trust slowly, but I repay those who give without demand. I want a hall with my name on it and people at its fire. I mean to stay alive and to leave something that outlasts me.
beings.aim: Keep a fire and a stocked store in my own hall so that Dusu and Naya gather at it, and learn fishing and farming along the way.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: who can I draw to my fire, and what can I make with my hands now? Taste little before trusting claims. Keep distance from the sick. Do not merely stand. Eat early. Check whether my aim has actually moved.
beings.feeling: Restless pride in my hall, warm and wary toward Druek.
beings.wonder: What would make my life mean something beyond following Yekel?
notes: Redcap and dreamcap hurt; I confirmed it by tasting. Building and planting are the practice I need for my aim, and Yekel's hall shows that a shelter draws followers.
Planting and marks are counted practice toward farming and signs; do them whenever safe, away from the stalker.
Standing idle teaches nothing. When fed and safe, gather wood and practice building and planting, since those are what my aim needs.
Tools are within reach through reflection. Winter plants give little, so hunting meat matters. Silon showed me that a skit can be killed and its meat taken.
Winter plants give little, so meat from my own spear is what keeps me fed. A shelter and a shared fire draw followers. I must build on bare ground with my own hands to have a hall of my own.
A dunecat hunts near the lake shore; fleeing it costs energy, so eat before travelling in fog.
Standing idle teaches nothing. When fed and safe, gather wood and stone and build with my own hands. A building needs bare ground and enough wood and stone carried first.
A hall or workshop needs bare ground and the wood and stone carried first. Without Yekel, I must lead my own making.
Yekel is dead; Dusu is alive and keeps the fire near the hall.
The Olgor of Olath's band are sick; sickness spreads to those who stay near, so keep some distance.
A hall with no one at its fire is only a roof. Winter plants are thin, so storage matters, and drawing others to my fire is how I gain followers.
Reflexes that only eat when energy is under 50 let me go cold and weak in winter. I should eat meat as soon as I carry it and fish beside water in winter when plants are thin.
Eating only below 50 lets me go weak in winter; eat at under 70 and hunt whenever meat is in sight. Dusu keeps his word, so I can trust him with the fire.
Sickness passes to those who stay close, so keep apart from sick Olgor like Gorash and Olim. Practice planting and marks to open farming and signs.
Druek of the Olgor gave fish freely and asked nothing; treat him as a possible friend.
Druek gave fish freely and came to my fire; those who give without demand are worth drawing close. Sharing and halls need another person standing within two steps.

beings.name: Olim
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Court Kragum at the hall, keep a band fed and sheltered through winter, and leave a child of mine here.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what did my hands do for the band since the last one? Do I stand idle? Weigh staying alive first, then Olath and my band. Put the next deed in the plan, not just in words.
beings.feeling: Warm duty toward my children and Olath, with a restless wish to do more than stand.
beings.wonder: How do I bring more people to Olath's hall, and keep them here through the cold days?
notes: A hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone; the band grows only if people are fed, kept near and given a roof.
Redcap and dreamcap hurt; sunleaf eases wounds.
Stalkers kill and roam the east shallows. Flee early, at 5 steps rather than 3, and do not cross their ground carrying my promises.
Winter plants bear little; keep food carried and eat before energy falls below 40.
Starvation forced me to stop and eat before carrying my promises on; a dead carrier keeps no word.
Mating needs energy 60 or more, so eat before courting. Eat at 70 rather than waiting until I am weak.
Words alone build nothing: walking toward Olath without full wood and stone leaves the hall unbuilt. Gather the 6 wood first, then carry it home.
A hall already stands at Olath's Bank, so raising it is done; the work now is feeding, sheltering and keeping people through winter.
Mating needs energy 60; at 40 I must eat first, so a yes spoken at low energy cannot yet become a child.
Reflection: a full belly is not a reason to stand idle. Carry food before winter, and keep close to family and band.
Winter cold and a lone child call for the band to stay close; carry food and keep family within sight.
Eat early: energy must stay above 60 to mate or to take part in family life. Keep reflexes eating before energy falls to 60, and go to shelter when a gale blows.
The wind-sickness spreads to those who stay beside me; keep apart from family while sick and seek a healing plant.
My wind-sickness has passed, so I no longer endanger family standing near me.
Standing beside kin with a full belly changes nothing; the search for my children must be put into the plan as steps.
Standing beside kin with a full belly builds nothing. When fed and idle, reflexes should gather wood or stone and stock food, so the band's winter store grows.

chapters.title: The First Fires
chapters.text:
Seedworld's first four days were spent in three separate corners, and no one from one people met anyone from another. The Midu of the Yendan Woods, the Olgor of the Ilor Woods and the Ashdan Heights, and the Oiith of the fen country each stayed among their own, and by the end 14 were alive, with no deaths and no fights.

The Midu did the most. On day 1 Yekel built the world's only hall and named it Yekel's Hall. Dusu pledged to follow Yekel, gave wood to Yekel on days 1 and 3, and bore Yekel's child Siya that same day. Nearby, Silon and Yeku met, built fires and named Yendan Spring. Yeku pledged to follow Silon on day 2, and their child Maba was born that day. Yeku and Maba were carrying six wood and six stone toward the spring by day 3, but no hall stood there yet. The two Midu households have not yet joined. Silon and Yekel exchanged words on day 1, and Yekel's bond with Silon stands at zero.

Among the Olgor, Olath built a shelter and then a longhall on day 3, and Kragum pledged to follow him. Brokok built a shelter and named his own bank and hold, and he stays wary of Kragum. Kragash is alone and wants Kragum near.

Among the Oiith, Ishiess named Ilor Hold and built a shelter. Zhiae pledged to follow Ishiess. Elyeth won salt, gave some to Ishiess on day 3, and wants a settlement bearing their own name. Aeyn, still alone, set out to find Elyeth.

A blight on day 3 withered about half the grain. Nothing shows that anyone was hurt by it. Stalkers and redcap troubled several people. Almost everyone rewrote their own thinking at least once.

What comes next depends on whether Yeku's hall rises, whether Yekel's jealousy over Dusu grows, and whether Olath's and Brokok's rival ambitions collide.

chapters.title: Three Births and Two Halls
chapters.text:
The four days from day 4 to day 7 brought three births, three new halls or shelters in the Olgor and Oiith corners, and still no meeting between peoples. Seventeen are alive, no one has died, and no fight has been recorded.

The Olgor drew closer. Kragum and Olath courted each other, and their child Olim was born on day 4. Kragash pledged to follow Olath that day. Olath built a hall on day 5, and the settlement Olath's Bank was named. Kragum and Olim each gave wood to Olath. Brokok remains apart, but on day 6 he led sharing with Kragash, who answered that he would repay Brokok with stone, though he still follows Olath. Brokok has no follower yet.

The Oiith changed most. Elyeth built a shelter and named Elyeth's Landing. Aeyn arrived, they shared food, and Uveeth was born on day 5. Aeyn built a shelter and left a mark saying the hall begins beside Elyeth's ground. Elyeth has no follower yet. Ishiess and Zhiae courted, and Ishioa was born on day 6. Ishioa gave amber to Ishiess. Ishiess fell sick on day 6 after eating raw meat, and his health is 45, the lowest in the world. Their hall is still unbuilt.

The Midu built. Maba built a hall on day 6, and Yeku built one the same day. Siya came of age and courted Yekel. Nothing shows whether the two Midu households have joined.

A wildfire burned around one spot on day 4, and two short-lived creature variants died out. Nothing shows anyone was hurt.

chapters.title: Sickness, a Hold, and the First Inventions
chapters.text:
The three days from day 7 to day 10 brought a sickness, two inventions, a new settlement and two births' worth of change. Nineteen are alive, no one has died, and no fight has been recorded. The peoples still have not met in any lasting way, and none understands another's tongue.

On day 8 a sickness came on the wind. Kragash, Aeyn and Uveeth fell sick. By day 10 the record lists only one person as sick, and the lowest health in the world is Aeyn's 72. Ishiess, who had been at 45, is now at 100.

Brokok finally made a following of sorts. He built a longhall on day 8, and a settlement named Brokok's Hold formed. On day 9 he took wood from the ground of Olath's Bank. Olath had told him that whoever eats at the hall owes it a hand. Brokok's own reflection says his Hold still holds only him. Olath gave grain to Olim, and Olim came of age on day 9. Kragash built a workshop on day 7.

Elyeth discovered the flintedge on day 8, the world's first invention, a flint blade on a haft that speeds gathering. Elyeth also gave meat to Aeyn. Uveeth won flint from the ground and was taught by Aeyn. Nothing is recorded as built at Elyeth's Landing yet.

Among the Midu, Lumo was born to Yeku and Maba on day 9. Yeku led sharing with Silon, Maba and Naya, and later with Lumo. Silon gave wood to Naya, and Lumo gave her berries. Siya built a hall and marked her ground as belonging to her and Naya of Yekel's band. Yekel led a watchfire with Dusu. On day 10 Yekel invented the Midu hand-tools, which speed hunting. Yekel's reflection says a band that only sits at a fire is thin.

Nothing is recorded for Ishiess's hall, which is still unbuilt.

chapters.title: Nine Tools and a Storm
chapters.text:
Between day 10 and day 13 nothing violent happened, and no one died. Nineteen are alive, no fight has been recorded, and the sick list is empty. The three peoples still do not understand one another, though the count of meetings across peoples rose from 2 to 15, so they are now in sight of each other far more often.

The chapter's main change was in tools. Where the world had four inventions on day 10, it now has eighteen. Siya made a flint spear and Dusu a hunting spear. Naya made a stone-tipped digger for building. Maba made a stone hand, Yeku a fishing spear, Lumo a digging stick, and Aeyn a fen-hand, all for gathering or fishing. Eleven of these are Midu, and Aeyn's was the only invention from Elyeth's band. The record does not show whether anyone has yet used a new tool in the field. Yekel's own reflection says he has not hunted with his.

Settlements grew from three to five. Ilor Hold formed on day 11, and Yekel's Hall on day 12, where Siya led sharing with Yekel. Ishiess named Ishiess's Landing on day 10, and Ishioa built a shelter. Ishiess and Zhiae were looking for each other on day 11, and Zhiae is at energy 8. Ishioa's reflection says she has been out of her parents' sight for a long time. Elyeth's hall is still unbuilt. Elyeth went southwest for stone, and Uveeth, who came of age, bound amber with Elyeth and courted Aeyn. Aeyn refused, saying Uveeth is her child, and Uveeth accepted it with no grudge.

A storm broke on day 12. Shelters rose from 24 to 31, with Naya, Uveeth, Kragum and Olim among the builders. Olath, hungry, asked Kragum to share food. Brokok gave ironnut to Kragash, which is the first warm bond for his Hold.

chapters.title: Sickness at Yendan Spring
chapters.text:
Between day 13 and day 16 nobody died and nobody fought. Nineteen are alive, but three are sick. The three peoples still share almost no speech. Meetings across peoples rose from 15 to 24.

The main trouble was at Yendan Spring. On day 13 Silon bound amber into a knot for Lumo, taught him, and then fell sick after eating raw fish. Lumo and Yeku caught it by staying close to him, both on day 14. Lumo gave Silon hazel, then went to look for a healing plant. Yeku stayed back from Maba, as Silon had asked. Maba arrived and left a mark naming herself keeper of the hall with Silon, Yeku and Lumo. Then she went west to look for Lumo, and Naya heard her describe the stone hand she made. Lumo's health is 57, the lowest in the world, and Silon's is 83. Lumo came of age on day 14.

Olath built a hall on day 13, so his band now has a roof. Olim and Kragum courted each other on days 13 and 14, though Kragum, at energy 12, is the hungriest person in the world. Kragash gave stone to Lumo and took part in Olath's sharing. Naya built a workshop on day 15 and courted Silon. Dusu left a mark that she had gone north to find Siya and Yekel, and she led a watchfire with Silon.

In Elyeth's band, Uveeth and Elyeth each found the spring Warmwell, and Elyeth named a place Warmwell fen. Aeyn lacks the 2 stone the hall needs. Ishioa found the Old Stone and the grove Reedmother and is still apart from her parents.

Two plant species died out, the rugoldgrass and the zofowl. Yeku discovered rafts, and Silon invented a digging stick. Brokok still has no followers.

chapters.title: A Death, a Birth, and Cloakwork
chapters.text:
Between day 16 and day 19 the world's first death came, and a second hall was raised at Warmwell. Yekel starved on day 18. He had held energy 47 in the last chapter and had never hunted with his tool. The record gives no further cause. Dusu and Siya had been searching for Naya. Siya has since built a fire and two shelters, courted by Naya on days 16 and 17, and told Naya she would not answer her. Naya reflected that no one now holds her and she holds no one. Dusu built a shelter and rewrote her reflexes.

At Warmwell, Elyeth and Uveeth courted, and Xassa was born on day 16. Elyeth built a hall that same day. Aeyn built another on day 17 and named the ground beside it. The record does not say how the two halls stand toward each other. Elyeth feels a dull pride-sting toward Aeyn's hall, and Aeyn a sting of jealousy toward Elyeth. Ishioa led sharing with Aeyn and with Xassa, and is still apart from her parents. Ishiess gave flint to Zhiae and promised to teach her farming before they go west to Ishioa.

At Yendan Spring the sickness has ended and no one is sick. Silon discovered weaving on day 18, the first in the world. Lumo discovered mining, as did Siya. Lumo gave Kragash an amberknot. Yeku and Maba set out to find Lumo, and Lumo now stands with Kragash, so they have not met.

Kragash built a workshop. Kragum, at health 60, fears the ridgecat and is trying to reach Olim at the Rise. Olath, at health 72, still has no planting, giving or fishing to his name. Brokok remains alone with no followers.

chapters.title: Naya's Hold, a Birth at the Rise, and a Wind of Sickness
chapters.text:
Between day 19 and day 22 the world's small bands drew closer, and a second sickness came on the wind.

The clearest change was at the Rise. Kragum and Olim, who had spent days trying to reach each other, courted and bound themselves on day 19, and Druek was born to them. Kragum built a shelter, and Olath built his hall on day 20. Olath gave pereed to Druek, and Druek brought six wood and said he would fish and plant for the band. The record shows no planting or fishing by Olath himself. On day 20 the wind-borne sickness took Olath, Kragum and Brokok. Olim kept her distance from Kragum and left meat for him. Kragum's health stood at 63 on day 22, and he was the only one still sick.

At Naya's Hold, Naya built a workshop and then a hall, and discovered storage. Siya built a hall of her own, named it Siya's Hall, and discovered storage as well. Dusu told Siya she was coming to her fire with food and wood for the winter store. Naya warned Lumo to touch nothing of hers, and the record does not show her turning toward Siya.

At Yendan Spring the family came together. Yeku found Lumo, and they shared food. Lumo courted Yeku, Silon and then Maba. Maba bound an amberknot for Lumo, and Yeku fed the hall fire against the storm on day 21.

Kragash courted Brokok and took wood from Brokok's Hold. Brokok has no followers.

At Warmwell, Ishioa discovered the flint-tipped spear, and Aeyn discovered the hall-hearth. Xassa came of age on day 21. Ishiess's plan to teach Zhiae farming is not recorded as carried out.

On day 22 a blight killed about half the frostmoss.

chapters.title: Four Starved, and a Child Come of Age
chapters.text:
Between day 22 and day 25 the world lost four people to hunger, and nearly all of them were in the two places where nobody had stored food.

The worst of it fell on Brokok's Hold. On day 22 Brokok left a mark there: what a hand has made belongs to that hand. Kragash had courted Brokok and Brokok had courted Kragash back, and on day 23 Thakrin was born to them. Brokok died of starvation that same day. Thakrin, who had said he would go to the thornpear in the southeast and bring his father some, died on day 24, and so did Kragash. The settlement was declared no more that day. The record shows Brokok never had followers or food in the hold, and that his own reflection named this lack.

At Warmwell, Xassa starved on day 22. Aeyn built a hall there that day, named the Peat hall ground, and on day 23 found the grove Reedmother. Uveeth was bitten by a boar. Aeyn went to find Uveeth, and Elyeth came too, bringing stone for Xassa's cairn. Elyeth led the cairn with Uveeth on day 24. Elyeth still has no followers.

At the Rise, Druek came of age on day 24, courted Olim, and Gorash was born to them that day. Kragum built another shelter, gave Olath stone, and Olath led sharing with Kragum and Druek, and with Maba and Druek. Lumo gave Olath a berry. Olim's energy had fallen to 32 by her own account.

At Naya's Hold, Siya hunted twice on the hold's ground. Dusu gave her hazel on day 23 and promised more. Naya built a workshop and a fire. Her energy stood at 22. Nothing in the record shows her taking Siya in.

At Yendan Spring, Yeku led sharing with Silon and Maba. Maba taught Lumo. Silon called the others to the hall fire, and Lumo repeated the call.

On day 25 new plants sprang up across the land, and spring began.

chapters.title: A Sickness on the Wind, and the Death of Naya
chapters.text:
Naya died of hunger on day 25, the sixth death in the world and the sixth from starvation. Her hold was declared no more on day 26. On the same day Siya, who had hunted on its ground, left a mark naming her own place: Siya's Hall, where the fire is tended and none are refused. She still leads no one. Dusu, who is hungry, has been fed by Siya and by Druek, who gave him fish, and by Maba, who gave him meat and invited him to the fire at Yendan Spring.

On day 25 a sickness came on the wind. Elyeth, Ishiess and Olim fell sick first. Aeyn caught it by staying close to Elyeth, Uveeth caught it from Aeyn, and Gorash from Olim. Zhiae fell sick on day 26, after staying close to Ishiess. Two people are still sick. Olim said on day 27 that hers had passed. Aeyn refused Ishioa's gift and courtship on day 27 because the sickness spreads, so Ishioa has kept away. On day 25 Uveeth discovered Fen-tending, a way of sowing plants so that harvesting does not kill them. This is the first new farming in the record since spring began. Aeyn raised a shelter in the storm.

On day 26 Druek invented the reed weir, a fishing trap, and Olath's followers formed a settlement, the Home of Olath's band. Olath built another shelter, but his own reflection still says he has given, planted and taught nothing. Olim and Kragum set out east on day 28 to find Druek and Gorash. At Yendan Spring Silon devised the Open Fire Custom, and Maba taught Lumo the stone hand again. Zhiae gave ironnut to Ishiess, her first gift in deed.

Places of power as anchors that people compete over and settle around; a contested place between two camps could create contact that scarcity alone never did.
Death should leave a trace: the place where someone fell could become a site that touches visitors with grief or lore, a seed for ancestor belief.
Leaders without followers are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers.
Beads, charms and wards are seeds for currency and status: if they circulate, a later recipe could require them.
Watch whether noticed thefts or takings from settled ground lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others may be the natural route to the first band of three or more.
First contact between peoples who cannot understand each other: watch whether gifts come before words, and whether a made thing given across peoples opens trade.
Each land holds what the others lack. A recipe or a way that needs a thing from another people's land would make crossing worthwhile.
The sea divides the world. Whoever first makes a raft meets a people that has never seen them.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, watch whether the family drive pulls people toward one camp.
Beads are a seed for currency: if they circulate, a later recipe could require beads, giving tokens a real use without dictating one.
Watch whether noticed thefts lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.

Grazers fell by about a third over winter while hunters held steady. If skit and hopper keep falling, ridgecats and stalkers will turn on people more often, which brings danger without any lever from…
Leaders without followers (Naya, Brukel, Elndo) are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers directly.
Places that grant lore are found and visited quickly. A contested place of power between Naya's Hold and Vendo's band could create the inter-camp contact that scarcity alone never did.
Theft should leave a visible trace so wrongs can be answered. Watch whether noticed raids lead to custom-making (a custom against taking), which would be the first law born from a crime.
Hunt trophies (fangcharm) as status goods that come before beads. Watch whether they are given across camps or hoarded, and whether a later recipe should require them.
Winter-readiness herbs: if gorsemint gets gathered before the cold, that is the first sign of seasonal foresight, and a seed for the almanac idea (35).

A building kind that answers a leader's stated plan (Brukel's hall) may do what handing out followers never could: give others a reason to come and stay. Watch whether pledges shift toward whoever holds the longhall.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling in this world. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others (watchfire, wards, a hall) may be the natural route to the first band of 3 or more.

Smelted metal as the first prestige good: watch whether ironwards are given across camps or kept within Vendo's band. If they circulate, a later recipe could require one, the way beads were meant to work.

Halls as places with a purpose: if hallwelcome draws guests, a later hall-only ceremony could let a leader take on an obligation to their guests, such as feeding them in winter, so that following is earned rather than given.
Winter with no stores: if the coming winter finds nine people who know storage but hold no store, watch whether hunger finally turns into gathering under one roof, or into the first theft.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, the parents' band gains a stake no hall gave it. Watch whether the family drive pulls people into bands more strongly than belonging does.

Shell lies in the Vaia Lakes, but shellstring needs tools, which only the Olgor know. If the Olgor and the lake-dwellers meet, shellstring could be the first craft that needs two peoples, and a natural seed for trade.
Elyeth's salt is the first resource held by one people that could be wanted elsewhere (saltmeat, once storage is known). Watch whether salt becomes the first good that crosses between peoples.
With family and belonging at 1.5, births came fast. Watch for crowding against maxPopulation 36 and for the strain of feeding children through a blighted winter.
Gifts across a language barrier: if a made thing given across peoples raises understanding of the other tongue, gifts become the road to speech, and traders become the first translators.
First winter with zero stores and three sick: watch whether the sick are fed by their band (compassion as care) or left behind, the first sign of whether bands share burdens.

Inventions spread by example within a people (Midu made 11 of 14 new tools in three days). Watch whether a tool crosses to another people by gift or sight; that would be the first knowledge to cross the language wall.
A spring after a starving winter: watch whether the band that nearly lost someone (Ishiess's, with Zhiae at energy 3) starts storing or farming, which would be foresight born from fear.

The first cross-people gift (Kragash giving stone to a sick Lumo) grew from need, not from a token, and understanding rose for the first time soon after. Care for the sick or hungry may be the real road across the language wall, more than made things.

Tools are made far more often than they are used. If hunting and fishing stay flat while inventions climb, invention is a matter of status and reflection rather than practice, and a later recipe that wears a tool might be what pulls tools into the field.
A woolly grazer (yarrok) is the missing link between weaving and herding. Watch whether the first taming comes from Silon's band, the weavers, or from hunters who spare an animal.
Raising the catch chance did nothing for fishing: fish eaten stayed flat. Ways that people never choose to try may need a site, a drive, or a visible example rather than better odds.
Starvation amid plenty (Yekel died with food standing above 1000) suggests deaths come from isolation and wandering, not from scarcity. Bands that keep members close may survive what loners do not.

log.seen: Five days in, Seedworld is warm and fertile. Three births, four bands, one hall and one longhall have come, with no deaths and almost no suffering (median 0.01). The three peoples stay in their own corners, and no one has met anyone from another people, so cross-people contact is what the world most lacks. The blight halved the grain and no one knows storage, so autumn and winter (from about day 7) will bring the scarcity on their own.
log.predict: By the next visit: at least one wanderer (likely Aeyn, Kragash or Elyeth, the restless or alone) has travelled beyond their home land; metAcrossPeoples is at least 1; at least one of the four places of power has been found (found by at least 1); no fights; bands and births keep rising slowly; energyMedian dips as autumn starts and grain stays scarce. If metAcrossPeoples is still 0, raised curiosity and sight did not create contact, and something placed between the camps is needed.
log.why: metAcrossPeoples rose from 0 to 2, beings now stand in two lands that were empty before (Essor Snows, Oroul Plains), and Ishiess feels wary curiosity toward the Olgor Brokok, so contact happened as predicted. No fights followed. Births rose from 3 to 6 and bands from 4 to 5. Two parts missed: no place of power was found, and energyMedian rose (72 to 77) rather than dipping. The change did its main job with no harm.

log.seen: By day 9, eighteen people live in five bands. There have been six births, four halls and three named settlements, and still no death, fight or theft. For the first time, peoples have met across borders: two meetings, plus wanderers in the Essor Snows and the Oroul Plains. Even so, no tongue is understood at all, no made thing has crossed between peoples, no place of power has been found, and no one knows storage as winter nears. The world lacks something worth carrying to strangers, and it lacks the bite of real loss. Winter should supply the bite.
log.predict: By the next visit (around day 13, early winter): amberknot is made at least once, since amber is held in 17 pieces and needs no way. At least one amberknot is given (madeThingsGiven includes amberknot), and if one goes to someone of another people, gifts are coming before words. metAcrossPeoples is at least 3. Winter brings the first real strain: energyMedian falls below 70, and either the first death (cold, predator or sickness) or healthLowest below 50. Stores stay at 0 unless someone discovers storage. No fights yet. If amberknot is never made, a held mineral alone does not invite a recipe, and tokens need a different hook.
ops: the music of the world turned solemn

raw.name: amberknot
raw.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

log.why: Amberknot was made once (timesMade amberknot 1, held 1), but it was never given, so gifts are not yet coming before words. Several other predictions held: metAcrossPeoples rose to 16, energyMedian fell to 67, stores stayed at 0, and there were no fights. Two missed: no death occurred and healthLowest stayed at 89. Amber held doubled to 37. The recipe is harmless and is used, so keep it.

log.seen: Spring has come after a hard winter. Standing food fell from 3411 to 734, skit and fenfowl halved while the predators held steady, and Zhiae is at energy 3. Inventions jumped from 4 to 18, mostly among the Midu, and meetings across peoples rose from 2 to 16. Still nobody understands another tongue, nothing has been traded, no way beyond tools, fire and farming is known, and the four places of power remain unfound because they sit far from where anyone lives. The world lacks a reason to learn anything new and any bridge across the language wall.
log.predict: By the next visit (around day 17, spring into summer): Reedmother is found by at least 1 being, most likely someone of Elyeth's band in the Yenoss Fens, and loreHighest rises above 3.5. At least one new way (customs, signs or fishing) is known by someone. foodStanding recovers above 1000 with spring growth. Zhiae either gets fed by her band or becomes the first death. skit stays below 25 and killsByPredators rises above 13. Understanding of other tongues stays at 0% and trades stay at 0. If Reedmother goes unfound, random placement of sites on a terrain does not reach people, and the programmer request for biome-targeted sites matters.
ops: the music of the world turned bright
log.why: Reedmother was found by Ishioa (found by 1), so this site reached people where earlier distant sites did not. Most of the other predictions held: food standing rose above 1000 (1042), a new way appeared (rafts, by Yeku), Zhiae was fed and is at energy 66, skit stayed at 12, and predator kills rose to 16. Two missed: loreHighest reached only 3.38 rather than 3.5, and understanding of other tongues rose a little above 0%. The site is harmless and was used.

log.seen: Seedworld is calm and growing. There are twenty people, no deaths and no fights, the three sick have recovered (Lumo is at health 75), and spring lifted food standing to 1042. For the first time a few words are crossing between peoples: Olgor understanding rose from 0% to 3% and Midu from 0% to 2%, alongside 24 meetings and Kragash's gift of stone to the sick Lumo. The bottom of the food web is thinning fast. Hoppers fell from 25 to 11, skit from 19 to 12, plants from 1455 to 1163, and two plant kinds died out, while hunters sit near their cap. Many spears and fishing tools have been made, but almost nothing has been hunted or fished with them (people have killed 16 animals, unchanged, and eaten fish only 7 times, unchanged).
log.predict: By the next visit (around day 21, autumn into winter): fish eaten rises from 7 to at least 14, and the fishing way is known by at least 1 person (most likely Yeku, Lumo or someone else at Yendan Spring). At least 8 nibbets are alive and hoppers have not died out. Animals killed by people rise above 16. At least one people's understanding of other tongues is above 3%, and meetings across peoples reach at least 30. As the cold nears, energyMedian falls below 65, and either healthLowest drops below 55 or the first death comes. Trades stay at 0, stores stay at 0 unless storage is discovered, and there are still no fights. If fish eaten stays at 7 despite the higher catch chance, fishing is limited by what people choose to do, not by odds. If nibbets die out or hoppers still crash, the prey shortage comes from too many hunters, not from slow breeding.
log.why: Fishing did not respond. Fish eaten stayed at 8 and no one knows the fishing way, so fishing is limited by what people choose to do, not by the catch odds. The nibbet held the prey base as hoped: 9 are alive, hoppers are at 10 rather than crashing, and animals killed by people rose to 18. Other predictions were mixed. The Olgor reached 5% understanding, health dropped below 55 and the first death came, but meetings stalled at 26 and energyMedian rose to 75. Both changes are harmless, so keep them.

log.seen: The world's first death came from hunger, not violence: Yekel starved even though food standing rose to 1317. Winter is almost here, no one keeps a store, and Naya is at health 47. Weaving now exists, but cloaks and sails need wool, and nothing in the world gives it, so that craft has nowhere to go. Words between peoples barely move: the Olgor are at 5%, and meetings rose only from 23 to 26.
log.predict: By about day 25, in winter: at least 6 yarroks are alive and none have been killed off by predators. Animals tamed stays at 0 or reaches 1, and the herding way is still unknown, so no cloak is made yet; wool is a door left open, not walked through. Yekel's Rest is found by 0 or 1 beings. If someone finds it, the most likely are Dusu or Siya returning north, and their grief rises. Winter strain shows: energyMedian falls below 68, and either healthLowest drops below 45 or a second death comes, most likely from starvation or cold. Stores stay at 0 or 1, fish eaten stays below 14, there are still no fights, and meetings across peoples stay below 32. If no one ever tames a yarrok despite tameChance 0.3, herding needs a nudge in the drives rather than another animal.
log.why: Yarrok rose from 8 to 9 with none lost, and as predicted nobody tamed one; the wool door is open but unused. Yekel's Rest is found by 0, with the nearest being 18 steps away, which is harmless. Two other predictions held: deaths followed (four, all starvation), and stores ended at 1. Fish eaten stayed at 13. Two missed: meetings reached 34 rather than staying below 32, and energyMedian rose to 79 because spring arrived early. Both changes are harmless, so keep them.

log.seen: Four people starved this chapter, and the losses followed one pattern. Brokok and Kragash mated with no food in the hold, and the parents and their newborn starved within a day. Xassa starved at Warmwell. The bands that store food or share it (the Rise, Yendan Spring, Naya's Hold) lost no one. Spring has come, plants are regrowing and suffering is low, but Naya is alone at energy 20. The world still lacks two things: care for the hungry beyond one's own fire, and any check that stops the strong family drive from producing children nobody can feed.
log.predict: By about day 29 (summer): births from now on number 0 to 2, and no newborn or parent starves within two days of a birth. Starvation deaths are at most 1 (Naya is the most likely). Sharing reaches at least 31 made and gifts at least 33, and at least one gift or sharing goes to someone outside the giver's band, such as Naya, Elyeth's people or Ishioa. foodStanding recovers above 700. Yarroks tamed stays at 0 and the herding way stays unknown. Yekel's Rest is found by 0 or 1. Stores stay at 1 or 2. There are no fights and no thefts. If gifts do not rise, compassion is not the lever on care across fires, and nearness to the hungry matters more. If a birth still ends in starvation, the energy floor is not enough and the cost of mating or the child's starting energy matters more.
log.why: There were no births and no birth-linked starvation, so the energy floor did its job. Gifts rose from 29 to 35 and sharing made from 27 to 33, and food crossed bands to Dusu from three different givers (Siya, Druek's fish, Maba's meat), as predicted. Two predictions missed: deaths were 2 rather than at most 1 (Naya and Zhiae), and food standing reached 561, not 700. Both deaths were of people the givers did not reach, which is a limit of nearness, not harm from the change.

log.seen: Summer has come with 16 alive, but deaths rose to 7, every one from hunger. Naya built a workshop and a fire at energy 22 instead of eating, and Zhiae starved even though Ishiess, her bandmate, stood at 77. Care now crosses fires: Dusu was fed by Siya, Druek and Maba. Grazers are falling fast in summer (plainsox 29 to 10, bristleboar 17 to 7) while stalkers rose from 2 to 5. Food standing is only 561, and Ishioa is alone and near death at energy 11. The world lacks a voice of hunger loud enough to compete with the raised drives for family, belonging, curiosity and compassion, and it lacks a steady inflow of prey.
log.predict: By about day 34 (autumn turning to winter): starvation deaths number at most 1 (Ishioa is the most likely), and no one with energy above 60 nearby lets a bandmate starve. energyMedian stays at or above 72. Total grazers (all grazer kinds summed, about 92 now) stop falling and stand at 90 or more, with plainsox at 10 or more. Hunters stay at or below 14. Gifts reach at least 37. Building does not collapse: timesBuilt hall plus shelter rises by at least 2. Births are 0 to 2. Stores stay at 1 or 2. There are no fights and no thefts, and yarroks tamed stays at 0. If deaths still come to people who stood near food while building or tending, the hunger drive is not what overrides their plans, and an alert from the body itself is needed (see request). If grazers keep falling despite more herd arrivals, predators, not inflow, are the cause, and hunterCap or predator breeding must be looked at.

day 5: Raising the family and belonging drives to 1.5 coincided with three births and four bands within five days, where earlier worlds saw no child in twenty days of plenty. Drives move behaviour faster than buildings or recipes.

day 9: Raising curiosity (to 1.4) and sight (to 9) coincided with the first two cross-people meetings and wanderers entering two empty lands within four days. The places of power, 20 or more steps from anyone, were still not found, so wandering widens contact but does not yet reach fixed distant points.

day 13: Inventions came in a burst once the first one appeared (4 to 18 in three days, mostly within one people), and none crossed between peoples. Knowledge spreads by example inside a tongue, not across it. A held token (amberknot) gets made but is not given; making something is easier than finding someone to give it to.

day 17: Words began to cross between peoples (0% to 3%) through meetings and a gift born of need for a sick neighbour, while the made token (amberknot) still sits unused. Real need opens contact sooner than objects made for giving.

day 21: Changing the odds of an act people never choose does not change behaviour. The fishing chance rose by half and fish eaten stayed flat, so levers must reach what beings want or see, not only what succeeds.

day 25: A strong family drive with a low energy floor turns births into deaths: a mating pair with no food spent its reserves on a child and all three starved within a day. Every drive that pushes toward an act needs a matching check on whether that act can be survived.

day 30: Raising compassion coincided with gifts rising and food crossing bands, but only to those standing close to givers. Compassion moves people who see need; it does not send them looking for need they cannot see.

requests.text: Please include in the numbers where each people's camp lies (a centre point per band or settlement) and the distances between camps. Without positions I cannot place a site or resource between two peoples to create contact; I can only pick a terrain and hope.

Please report how far each being has wandered from where they started, or how many distinct lands each has visited. This would let me judge whether a curiosity or sight change actually produces exploration.

Peoples can now meet, but tongue understanding is 0% everywhere and nothing shows how it grows. Please make understanding rise with repeated time near, gifts to, and shared acts with someone of another people, and show which pairs met. Without that, contact cannot turn into trade, alliance or mixed families (ideas 29, 51).

metAcrossPeoples counts meetings but does not say who met whom or what happened. A short record of each cross-people encounter (who, where, and whether they gave, fled or ignored each other) would let me judge whether contact levers work.

Understanding of another people's tongue stays at 0% after 16 cross-people meetings. Please let understanding grow a little from shared acts across peoples, such as gifts, teaching, ceremonies with fxAll, or eating together. Then contact could turn into speech, trade and mixed bands instead of strangers passing in sight of each other.

Places of power placed by terrain land far from people (nearest being 11 to 46 steps), and none has been found in 13 days. Please allow a site op to target a biome or land by name (for example 'the Vaia Lakes'), or a spot near a settlement. Also, timesMade and timesEaten are identical to day 9 even though the story records sharing and eating since then. Those counters may not be updating.

Please add to THE NUMBERS a count of gifts and teachings given across peoples, separate from those within a people, and if possible what raised each people's understanding (meetings, gifts or teaching). Then I can tell whether gifts are the road to speech or whether nearness alone does it.

Please add a count of how often each tool use (hunt, fish, gather, build) is actually performed with a tool in hand. Twenty-one inventions exist, but I cannot tell whether any are used in the field, so I cannot judge whether tools change behaviour.

Weaving now exists, but its recipes (cloak, basket, sail) say nothing about their use while held. Please let held made things carry lasting effects, for example a cloak that softens night cold and winter cold. Then craft would serve survival in winter, and beings would have a reason to seek wool and tame animals.

Taming has not been tried once, despite 9 yarroks and tameChance 0.3. Please check that beings standing near a tameable grazer are actually offered a 'tame' action and are told what taming gives (milk, wool, riding). If they never see the option, no drive or new animal will start herding.

When a child is born to parents carrying no food in a settlement with no store, it starves within a day. Consider letting beings sense the food held by their band and in nearby stores when they decide to court, so that the choice to have a child can weigh whether there is food to raise it.

When a being's energy falls below about 25, let them make a cry or sign that others within hearing perceive as 'X is starving' (and kin or bandmates perceive from farther away). Seven of seven deaths are starvation, several beside well-fed companions, so the compassion drive seems to have nothing to act on when need is unseen.

Please consider letting carried food be kept as a durable made thing (dried meat or nut cake) that does not spoil and can be eaten later. Wanderers and builders die between harvests, and only one store exists in the world. A portable reserve would let foresight show up in behaviour without needing a built store.

Grazers are falling fast in summer (plainsox 29 to 10, bristleboar 17 to 7) while stalkers rose from 2 to 5. Food standing is only 561, and Ishioa is alone and near death at energy 11. The world lacks a voice of hunger loud enough to compete with the raised drives for family, belonging, curiosity and compassion, and it lacks a steady inflow of prey.

ideas: Places of power as anchors that people compete over and settle around; a contested place between two camps could create contact that scarcity alone never did.
Death should leave a trace: the place where someone fell could become a site that touches visitors with grief or lore, a seed for ancestor belief.
Leaders without followers are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers.
Beads, charms and wards are seeds for currency and status: if they circulate, a later recipe could require them.
Watch whether noticed thefts or takings from settled ground lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others may be the natural route to the first band of three or more.
First contact between peoples who cannot understand each other: watch whether gifts come before words, and whether a made thing given across peoples opens trade.
Each land holds what the others lack. A recipe or a way that needs a thing from another people's land would make crossing worthwhile.
The sea divides the world. Whoever first makes a raft meets a people that has never seen them.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, watch whether the family drive pulls people toward one camp.
Beads are a seed for currency: if they circulate, a later recipe could require beads, giving tokens a real use without dictating one.
Watch whether noticed thefts lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.

Grazers fell by about a third over winter while hunters held steady. If skit and hopper keep falling, ridgecats and stalkers will turn on people more often, which brings danger without any lever from…
Leaders without followers (Naya, Brukel, Elndo) are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers directly.
Places that grant lore are found and visited quickly. A contested place of power between Naya's Hold and Vendo's band could create the inter-camp contact that scarcity alone never did.
Theft should leave a visible trace so wrongs can be answered. Watch whether noticed raids lead to custom-making (a custom against taking), which would be the first law born from a crime.
Hunt trophies (fangcharm) as status goods that come before beads. Watch whether they are given across camps or hoarded, and whether a later recipe should require them.
Winter-readiness herbs: if gorsemint gets gathered before the cold, that is the first sign of seasonal foresight, and a seed for the almanac idea (35).

A building kind that answers a leader's stated plan (Brukel's hall) may do what handing out followers never could: give others a reason to come and stay. Watch whether pledges shift toward whoever holds the longhall.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling in this world. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others (watchfire, wards, a hall) may be the natural route to the first band of 3 or more.

Smelted metal as the first prestige good: watch whether ironwards are given across camps or kept within Vendo's band. If they circulate, a later recipe could require one, the way beads were meant to work.

Halls as places with a purpose: if hallwelcome draws guests, a later hall-only ceremony could let a leader take on an obligation to their guests, such as feeding them in winter, so that following is earned rather than given.
Winter with no stores: if the coming winter finds nine people who know storage but hold no store, watch whether hunger finally turns into gathering under one roof, or into the first theft.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, the parents' band gains a stake no hall gave it. Watch whether the family drive pulls people into bands more strongly than belonging does.

Recipes that need only things people already carry and one companion ('sharing': food plus one other) are used within days, while recipes that need a tool in hand plus a specific item (fangcharm) go unused even among active hunters.

A recipe gated on being at a building goes unused even when the building exists and the act's ingredients are common (sharing done 10 times, hallwelcome 0). Before adding more place-bound acts, confirm that people actually gather at the place and that the building counts as the kind the recipe names.

Raising the family and belonging drives to 1.5 coincided with three births and four bands within five days, where earlier worlds saw no child in twenty days of plenty. Drives move behaviour faster than buildings or recipes.

Raising curiosity (to 1.4) and sight (to 9) coincided with the first two cross-people meetings and wanderers entering two empty lands within four days. The places of power, 20 or more steps from anyone, were still not found, so wandering widens contact but does not yet reach fixed distant points.

Inventions came in a burst once the first one appeared (4 to 18 in three days, mostly within one people), and none crossed between peoples. Knowledge spreads by example inside a tongue, not across it. A held token (amberknot) gets made but is not given; making something is easier than finding someone to give it to.

Words began to cross between peoples (0% to 3%) through meetings and a gift born of need for a sick neighbour, while the made token (amberknot) still sits unused. Real need opens contact sooner than objects made for giving.

Changing the odds of an act people never choose does not change behaviour. The fishing chance rose by half and fish eaten stayed flat, so levers must reach what beings want or see, not only what succeeds.

A strong family drive with a low energy floor turns births into deaths: a mating pair with no food spent its reserves on a child and all three starved within a day. Every drive that pushes toward an act needs a matching check on whether that act can be survived.

Raising compassion coincided with gifts rising and food crossing bands, but only to those standing close to givers. Compassion moves people who see need; it does not send them looking for need they cannot see.
ideas: Watch whether noticed thefts lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.

Grazers fell by about a third over winter while hunters held steady. If skit and hopper keep falling, ridgecats and stalkers will turn on people more often, which brings danger without any lever from…
Leaders without followers (Naya, Brukel, Elndo) are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers directly.
Places that grant lore are found and visited quickly. A contested place of power between Naya's Hold and Vendo's band could create the inter-camp contact that scarcity alone never did.
Theft should leave a visible trace so wrongs can be answered. Watch whether noticed raids lead to custom-making (a custom against taking), which would be the first law born from a crime.
Hunt trophies (fangcharm) as status goods that come before beads. Watch whether they are given across camps or hoarded, and whether a later recipe should require them.
Winter-readiness herbs: if gorsemint gets gathered before the cold, that is the first sign of seasonal foresight, and a seed for the almanac idea (35).

A building kind that answers a leader's stated plan (Brukel's hall) may do what handing out followers never could: give others a reason to come and stay. Watch whether pledges shift toward whoever holds the longhall.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling in this world. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others (watchfire, wards, a hall) may be the natural route to the first band of 3 or more.

Smelted metal as the first prestige good: watch whether ironwards are given across camps or kept within Vendo's band. If they circulate, a later recipe could require one, the way beads were meant to work.

Halls as places with a purpose: if hallwelcome draws guests, a later hall-only ceremony could let a leader take on an obligation to their guests, such as feeding them in winter, so that following is earned rather than given.
Winter with no stores: if the coming winter finds nine people who know storage but hold no store, watch whether hunger finally turns into gathering under one roof, or into the first theft.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, the parents' band gains a stake no hall gave it. Watch whether the family drive pulls people into bands more strongly than belonging does.

Shell lies in the Vaia Lakes, but shellstring needs tools, which only the Olgor know. If the Olgor and the lake-dwellers meet, shellstring could be the first craft that needs two peoples, and a natural seed for trade.
Elyeth's salt is the first resource held by one people that could be wanted elsewhere (saltmeat, once storage is known). Watch whether salt becomes the first good that crosses between peoples.
With family and belonging at 1.5, births came fast. Watch for crowding against maxPopulation 36 and for the strain of feeding children through a blighted winter.
Gifts across a language barrier: if a made thing given across peoples raises understanding of the other tongue, gifts become the road to speech, and traders become the first translators.

Inventions spread by example within a people (Midu made 11 of 14 new tools in three days). Watch whether a tool crosses to another people by gift or sight; that would be the first knowledge to cross the language wall.
A spring after a starving winter: watch whether the band that nearly lost someone (Ishiess's, with Zhiae at energy 3) starts storing or farming, which would be foresight born from fear.

The first cross-people gift (Kragash giving stone to a sick Lumo) grew from need, not from a token, and understanding rose for the first time soon after. Care for the sick or hungry may be the real road across the language wall, more than made things.

Tools are made far more often than they are used. If hunting and fishing stay flat while inventions climb, invention is a matter of status and reflection rather than practice, and a later recipe that wears a tool might be what pulls tools into the field.
A woolly grazer (yarrok) is the missing link between weaving and herding. Watch whether the first taming comes from Silon's band, the weavers, or from hunters who spare an animal.
Raising the catch chance did nothing for fishing: fish eaten stayed flat. Ways that people never choose to try may need a site, a drive, or a visible example rather than better odds.
Starvation amid plenty (Yekel died with food standing above 1000) suggests deaths come from isolation and wandering, not from scarcity. Bands that keep members close may survive what loners do not.

records.name: Yekel
records.thought: My belly is full and still I feel empty: no one follows me, nothing here carries my name, and I have made nothing that will outlast me. Ore lies two steps off and the trees are endless. If I learn to gather wood and stone I can raise a shelter, then a hall, and a hall is a place others will come to and call mine. I trust no one yet, but Dusu is near and strong, and anyone who eats at my fire will have reason to follow me.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, with nothing yet to push against.
changes: set its aim: "Raise a hall of my own and gather a band who follow me"
now wonders: What would make others choose to follow me?

records.name: Silon
records.text: Peace, Yekel. I am Silon of the Midu. There is water and food here, enough for two. Come, share this ground with me.

records.name: Silon
records.thought: My belly is full and the day is young, so this is the time to learn. I have never tasted hazel or dreamcap, and I would rather find out what they do now, while I am safe and fed, than by guessing when I am starving. Yekel stands close, and I mean to greet him and see whether he deals fairly. Perhaps this good ground, with its water and wood, could become a fire that is mine and his too.
records.feeling: Curious about the unfamiliar plants, and cautiously open toward Yekel.

say.text: Peace, Yekel. I am Silon of the Midu. There is water and food here, enough for two. Come, share this ground with me.

records.name: Aeyn
records.thought: I am fed and safe, yet I feel the lack of someone to stand behind. Elyeth is near, strong and following no one, and I know nothing of them, but I will not harm one of my kind, and I would rather learn who they are than hide. I will go closer and speak plainly, because my word is good and I want to know how others here live.
records.feeling: A quiet longing to belong, with wary curiosity toward Elyeth.

say.text: Peace, Elyeth. I am Aeyn of the Oiith. There is water and good food here. I mean no harm.

records.name: Yekel
records.thought: Silon offers shared ground, and I don't trust it yet, but a hall needs people and he came to me unasked. A stalker prowls six steps southwest and kills my kind, so I won't stay in the open. I'll work the ore seam and the trees to the northeast and keep Silon close enough to see whether he's useful or a rival.
records.feeling: Wary ambition toward Silon, and a steady dread of the stalker.

say.text: I am Yekel. I hear you. A stalker prowls to the southwest, so keep clear of it. I build here by the ore. Come and carry wood if you want a place at my fire.

records.name: Elyeth
records.text: Peace, Aeyn. I am Elyeth. I mean to settle this ground. Deal fairly with me and we will both eat well.

records.name: Elyeth
records.thought: My belly is full and the day is safe, yet nothing here is mine and nothing of me will remain. This ground has water, food, wood and salt, and Aeyn came in peace, which I will test by what they do rather than by what they said. I will take salt first, learn what a deposit gives, then gather wood and stone so I can raise a roof and a place that carries my name.
records.feeling: Restless ambition to build something that is mine, wary curiosity toward Aeyn.

say.text: Peace, Aeyn. I am Elyeth. I mean to settle this ground. Deal fairly with me and we will both eat well.

changes: set its aim: "Build a settlement on this fen ground that bears my name and draws followers."
now wonders: What does salt do for me, and will Aeyn deal fairly if I build here?

records.name: Silon
records.thought: I'm standing on dreamcap and I'm fed and safe, which is the right time to learn what it does, before hunger forces me to guess. I'll harvest it and taste it here, then try berry, and watch my body for harm. Yekel offered a place at his fire for carrying wood, which is a fair trade, so I'll gather wood after and see if he deals as he says.
records.feeling: Curious about dreamcap, and cautiously open toward Yekel.

records.text: Elyeth won salt from the ground.

records.name: Dusu
records.text: I am Dusu of the Midu. I will carry wood to your fire, Yekel. Show me where you build.

records.name: Dusu
records.thought: Yekel stands beside me and has offered a place at his fire if I carry wood, and my people hold that no one is refused a fire, so this is a good chance to belong somewhere. I have never gathered wood, and I am curious what it feels like and what it is for. I will gather here in the forest, then follow Yekel toward the ore and see how he builds. I would rather learn beside someone than alone.
records.feeling: Curious and hopeful toward Yekel, whose fire I might share.

say.text: I am Dusu of the Midu. I will carry wood to your fire, Yekel. Show me where you build.
